images.title: Why 87 passes the test for 3
images.purpose: Shows that each ten is 9 plus 1, so 87 leaves the same remainder on division by 3 as 8 + 7 = 15.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Two groups in one row, tens and ones, with the leftover sum underneath.
images.exact_structure: Group 1, labelled 8 tens above: 8 short teal (#0072B2) bars, each labelled 9, each with one small amber (#E69F00) square on top. Group 2, labelled 7 ones above: 7 small amber (#E69F00) squares in a row. 15 amber squares in all. Below, centred: 8 + 7 = 15. Under it, in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) box: 15 = 3 × 5, divisible by 3. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Nines are multiples of 3, so 87 is divisible by 3 because its digit sum 15 is.
images.description: Shows that each ten is 9 plus 1, so 87 leaves the same remainder on division by 3 as 8 + 7 = 15.
images.context: 87 = 8 × 9 + 15; 15 = 3 × 5; 87 = 3 × 29 (and 15 is not a multiple of 9, so 87 is not).

image_decisions.why: The same nines plus one picture, now judged by 3, shows why the digit sum works for 3 as well.
